# Follow-up fixes after DeepSeek Pro full review

Review only the committed range `7b288f070823df2b955200db7b9eb3f41f67f24f..e4814ef939f7596316aab6c44cf3e12d2f112316`, read-only. Start from the settled full-review findings:

1. Non-pure repeated calls were false V5 self-comparisons.
2. `toBe`/`strictEqual` incorrectly treated allocated object/array/regex literals as identical references.
3. Whitespace normalization collapsed distinct string-literal contents.

Their fixes and one additional wildcard fix are in this range:
- `87be1a7c` records exact literal spans and normalizes only code outside literals; six before-failing subcases now pass.
- `8afa3129` resolves known pytest and pytest.mark wildcard runtime suppressions; five before-failing subcases now pass.
- `5aef14d5` limits self-comparisons to side-effect-free operands, distinguishes identity from deep equality for allocated JavaScript literals, and handles redundant outer parentheses. Negative cases failed before and pass after; pure and deep-equality noops remain detected.

The final `e4814ef9` refactor preserves these behaviors while comparing source spans directly, sorting literal spans, and removing duplicate operand scanning. Its detector findings and behavior-preservation verification are settled; check this refactor as an additional attack surface rather than re-raising its rejected structural suggestions.

Verify those fixes against their tests, then look beyond them for concrete introduced defects. Check literal-span offsets, side-effect detection, identity versus deep equality, wildcard scoping, and baseline subtraction. Do not re-report the already tracked ledger correction or GitHub enforcement. Return at most three findings, or an empty findings list promptly.

summary: Reviewed the V5 self-comparison refactor and wildcard-pytest changes in scripts/check-verification-integrity.py. The literal-span/whitespace and side-effect fixes behave as their tests assert, but the new tagged-template suppression and the coarse object/array identity heuristic each introduce a concrete false negative: genuine always-true self-comparisons written with template literals or member accesses on allocated literals are no longer flagged, weakening the integrity gate.

findings.title: TAGGED_TEMPLATE regex suppresses plain (untagged) template-literal self-comparisons
findings.trigger: A new or weakened TypeScript test adds `assert.strictEqual(`x`, `x`)` or `expect(`x`).toBe(`x`)` — identical template literals with no interpolations.
findings.consequence: The V5 gate fails to flag the always-true self-comparison (false negative), so a constant assertion slips past verification-integrity; the identical expression was flagged before this change.
findings.evidence: self_comparing at scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:292 calls TAGGED_TEMPLATE.search(source.comparable[start:end]); the regex `[\w$)\]]\s*`` (line 274) also matches the closing backtick of a plain template because it is preceded by a word character. Verified: TAGGED_TEMPLATE.search('`x`') returns True, so self_comparing returns False for `assert.strictEqual(`x`, `x`)`.

findings.title: Identity check suppresses member accesses on object/array literals that evaluate to primitives
findings.consequence: These evaluate to `1 === 1` (always true) but are not reported as V5 (false negative). The equivalent regex access `assert.strictEqual(/a/.source, /a/.source)` is correctly flagged, showing the object/array branch is inconsistently coarse.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-verification-integrity.py:295 checks only the first character (`source.comparable[start] in "{["`), so any operand starting with `{` or `[` is treated as an allocated literal and skipped; the regex branch at line 297 instead requires `source.literals.get(start) == end` (the whole operand is the literal), which the object/array branch omits.
